_comment: Support settings for a stacked Gridfinity baseplate printed with a non-bonding interface filament (PETG). Pairs with a 0.2 mm gap: one interface layer. The film is then a single layer and tends to tear at the teeth -- the fringe of interface overhanging the rib, which prints as unsupported stubs. A 0.4 mm gap with two layers survives peeling but costs about 25 min. Pattern must stay concentric: it leaves 5 sub-2mm stubs where rectilinear leaves 65, and rectilinear_interlaced crashes the slicer outright at two interface layers. XY distance is the Bambu default 0.35, not the 0.8 measured earlier: 0.8 detaches the balconies from the socket walls, and a loose ribbon in an open cell makes more mess than an attached one. Once balconies are stripped from the G-code (ADR 0004), that trade goes away and 0.8 is worth revisiting.
